purpose: Capture weekly demand cycle
why_it_may_help: Sales differ systematically by day of week
evidence_from_eda: Weekend mean sales 1.361 vs weekday-only mean 1.038 units, a +31.1% difference (Phase 4). Consistent across all 3 categories (Phase 4 weekday x category table).
potential_risk_leakage: None - calendar date is known for the entire 28-day forecast horizon in advance.

purpose: Simplified binary version of day-of-week
why_it_may_help: Captures the dominant Sat/Sun step-change in one binary flag
evidence_from_eda: Same weekend vs weekday +31.1% evidence as day_of_week (Phase 4).
potential_risk_leakage: None - known in advance.

purpose: Capture broad seasonal (monthly) demand shifts
why_it_may_help: Some months sell more than others
evidence_from_eda: Highest month (Aug) vs lowest (Dec): 8.99% difference in mean sales (Phase 4). Real but modest compared to the weekday effect.
potential_risk_leakage: None - known in advance.

purpose: Finer-grained seasonal pattern than month
why_it_may_help: May capture within-month seasonal detail (e.g. late-summer peak around week 36)
evidence_from_eda: Mean sales range from 0.944 (week 52) to 1.231 (week 36) across the year (Phase 4) - about a 23% spread, but only 5 years of data to learn 52 levels from.
potential_risk_leakage: Risk of overfitting with high cardinality (52 levels) relative to only ~5 observed years per week. None from a pure availability standpoint - known in advance.

purpose: Capture long-run growth or decline
why_it_may_help: Long-term trend visible in daily totals
evidence_from_eda: Yearly total sales rose from 2011-2015 (Phase 4), but active-series count also rose from 16,762 to 30,474 over the same period - the apparent growth is at least partly a composition effect (more items listed), not proven organic per-item growth (Phase 4 composition check).
potential_risk_leakage: HIGH: raw categorical 'year' will contain values (2017+) never seen in training - cannot be used as a plain category. A continuous time index would generalize better but still risks conflating listing growth with real trend. Needs team discussion before use.

purpose: Capture most recent demand level
why_it_may_help: Yesterday's sales is the single strongest predictor found in this EDA
evidence_from_eda: Pearson r = 0.768 with same-day sales - the highest of all lags tested (Phase 9).
potential_risk_leakage: HIGH: only safe when computed relative to the forecast ORIGIN date, not per-target-day. In a direct 28-day-ahead model, 'lag_1 relative to each of the 28 target days' would require already knowing near-future sales - that is leakage. Safe only for a recursive (day-by-day) forecasting strategy or for the h=1 target.

purpose: Capture same-weekday demand a week ago
why_it_may_help: Controls for day-of-week while looking at recent history
evidence_from_eda: Pearson r = 0.720 with same-day sales (Phase 9).
potential_risk_leakage: Same origin-relative caveat as lag_1 - safe only relative to the forecast origin or within a recursive strategy.

purpose: Capture bi-weekly demand echo
why_it_may_help: Secondary recent-history signal
evidence_from_eda: Pearson r = 0.689 with same-day sales (Phase 9).
potential_risk_leakage: Same origin-relative caveat as lag_1/lag_7.

purpose: Capture demand from exactly one horizon-length ago
why_it_may_help: The only single lag that is naturally available for EVERY one of the 28 target days from a fixed origin
evidence_from_eda: Pearson r = 0.672 with same-day sales - still strong despite the longer gap (Phase 9).
potential_risk_leakage: LOW leakage risk when defined as (origin date - 28 days) and held constant across the whole 28-day horizon - this is the safest lag for a direct multi-horizon model.

purpose: Smooth recent noise into a stable demand-level estimate
why_it_may_help: Strongest single relationship found in this entire EDA
evidence_from_eda: Pearson r = 0.820 with same-day sales - higher than any raw lag (Phase 9).
potential_risk_leakage: HIGH: must be computed using only days up to and including the forecast origin, then held constant across all 28 target days - never recomputed using dates inside the forecast horizon.

purpose: Longer-window stable demand-level estimate
why_it_may_help: Nearly as strong as the 7-day window and more stable for sparse series
evidence_from_eda: Pearson r = 0.807 with same-day sales (Phase 9).
potential_risk_leakage: Same as rolling_mean_7 - origin-only window required.

purpose: Capture recent demand volatility
why_it_may_help: Series volatility varies a lot (per-series coefficient of variation), which plain mean-based features do not capture
evidence_from_eda: Series-level CV is highly dispersed - a meaningful share of series have CV > 2 (Phase 2, series_level_sales_stats.csv). Not yet correlated directly against sales in this EDA.
potential_risk_leakage: Same origin-only window requirement as the rolling means. Not yet evidence-tested for direct correlation with the target - flagged for follow-up.

purpose: Capture how long a series has been in a dry spell
why_it_may_help: The single cleanest relationship found in the whole EDA
evidence_from_eda: P(sale today) falls from 65.2% (sold yesterday) to 38.3% (1-3 days dry) to 22.2% (4-7) to 12.7% (8-14) to 6.2% (15-28) to 0.6% (29+ days dry) - a near-monotonic staircase (Phase 9).
potential_risk_leakage: LOW risk if computed strictly using history up to the origin date (a simple running count, no future data involved).

purpose: Same underlying signal as days_since_last_sale in run-length form
why_it_may_help: Directly usable for intermittent-demand-aware modeling approaches
evidence_from_eda: Zero-run lengths are highly right-skewed: median 2 days, mean 6.08 days, p99 = 52 days, max 1845 days (Phase 3). Streak length varies meaningfully by category/department (Phase 3, zero_streak_by_department.csv).
potential_risk_leakage: Same as days_since_last_sale - must use only pre-origin history.

feature: recent_nonzero_rate (e.g. pct nonzero days in last 28, as of origin)
purpose: Capture a series' recent activity level in a single normalized number
why_it_may_help: Complements rolling_mean by focusing on frequency rather than volume - useful for very low-volume series where the mean is close to zero anyway
evidence_from_eda: Directly related to the per-series zero% distribution documented in Phase 3 (mean 68.0%, std 22.3%, full distribution in series_zero_pct.csv).
potential_risk_leakage: LOW risk if computed on a trailing window ending at the origin (not the full series).

purpose: Assign each series to a broad demand-regularity segment for potential hierarchical or segment-specific modeling
why_it_may_help: Series behave very differently and this groups them
evidence_from_eda: 7,629 series are 'High-activity', 15,267 'Regular/intermittent', 6,103 'Sparse', 1,491 'Extremely sparse' (Phase 3 classification, thresholds at the p25/p75/p95 of the zero% distribution).
potential_risk_leakage: HIGH risk if computed using the ENTIRE series history (including the forecast period) - must be computed using only history available up to the origin date to avoid leaking the target period's own behavior into its own segment label.

purpose: Direct price-demand relationship
why_it_may_help: Price is one of the few genuinely forward-known variables in this dataset
evidence_from_eda: sell_prices.csv covers weeks beyond the processed table's last day (d_1941) per the processing report - Walmart prices are set in advance.
potential_risk_leakage: LOW leakage risk (price is legitimately known ahead of time) BUT this processed dataset (sales_long_full.parquet) does not yet include the future weeks' prices - a separate join against sell_prices.csv for the forecast horizon would be needed.

purpose: Normalize price within an item so cross-item scale differences don't dominate
why_it_may_help: Shows a much clearer relationship with demand than raw price once item scale is controlled for
evidence_from_eda: Mean sales by relative-price bin: 2.34 units at <0.85x the item's own average price, falling to 1.29 units at 1.0-1.05x, before an unexplained uptick at 1.05-1.15x (1.56) (Phase 7). Directionally consistent with basic price-demand intuition for the common range, but not perfectly monotonic - flagged for team discussion.
potential_risk_leakage: HIGH risk if the 'item's own average price' is computed over the FULL series history (including the forecast period) - must use an expanding or trailing average computed only from history up to the origin.

purpose: Test whether a recent price move is associated with a demand shift
why_it_may_help: Hypothesized demand-shock signal in the absence of an explicit promotion field
evidence_from_eda: Sales rose both after price INCREASES (+70.98% mean, Phase 7) and after price DECREASES (+48.47% mean, Phase 7), while the MEDIAN change in both directions was 0%. This pattern is inconsistent with a simple 'lower price leads to more sales' story and suggests price changes often co-occur with other demand-moving events rather than causing the lift themselves.
potential_risk_leakage: MEDIUM: this is a correlational, exploratory finding only - there is no promotion field to confirm causality. Using it as a hard feature risks encoding a spurious/confounded signal. Must be clearly labeled a hypothesis if used.
priority: Low (as a direct feature) / worth further investigation

purpose: Capture the large, event-specific effects the aggregate event flag hides
why_it_may_help: Individual named events have very large and very different effects that a single binary flag averages away
evidence_from_eda: Christmas -99.95% vs local baseline, Thanksgiving -29.9%, NewYear -20.4%, Mother's day -12.5%, but LaborDay +27.5%, ColumbusDay +9.6% (Phase 5, event_name_aggregated_lift.csv, 30 named events).
potential_risk_leakage: None - the calendar (including all events) is known for the entire 28-day forecast horizon in advance.

purpose: Simple flag for 'something calendar-notable is happening'
why_it_may_help: Cheap baseline event signal
evidence_from_eda: Weak in aggregate: event-day mean sales are actually 4.6% LOWER than non-event days overall (Phase 5) - masking the large but offsetting effects of individual events (some strongly negative like Christmas, some positive like LaborDay).
potential_risk_leakage: None - known in advance. Low standalone value given how much it averages away; better used alongside event_name.

purpose: Group events into broad types (Sporting/Cultural/National/Religious)
why_it_may_help: Coarser grouping that might generalize better to rare events than exact event_name
evidence_from_eda: Mean sales by type: Sporting 1.174, Cultural 1.139, Religious 1.129, National 0.966 vs non-event baseline 1.135 (Phase 5) - a real but modest spread.
potential_risk_leakage: None - known in advance.

purpose: Capture pre/post-event demand build-up or hangover
why_it_may_help: Some holiday shopping patterns build up over several days rather than landing only on the exact date
evidence_from_eda: Not directly tested in this EDA - flagged as an untested hypothesis for follow-up analysis before adoption.
potential_risk_leakage: None expected (calendar-derived), but the underlying effect is UNVERIFIED - do not treat as evidenced until tested.

feature: snap indicator (state-specific: snap_CA/snap_TX/snap_WI matched to the row's own state)
purpose: Capture the state-level SNAP benefit calendar's effect on food spending
why_it_may_help: SNAP effect is real, sizeable, and concentrated exactly where it should be (food)
evidence_from_eda: Overall SNAP-day sales +12.7% vs non-SNAP (Phase 6). Effect is strongest in FOODS (+17.3%) and specifically FOODS_2 (+32.3%), much weaker in HOBBIES (+2.5%) and HOUSEHOLD (+3.5%) - a pattern that matches how SNAP benefits are actually meant to be used, a good internal consistency check (Phase 6).
potential_risk_leakage: None - the SNAP calendar is published in advance, same as other calendar fields.

purpose: Distinguish genuine pre-listing 'not yet available' periods from ordinary intermittent demand
data_source: sales_long_full.parquet (self) - first date with a non-null sell_price
why_it_may_help: Strong, specific evidence that leading zero-runs are structurally different from later zero-runs
evidence_from_eda: For series with a leading zero block, the gap until first sale lines up almost exactly with the gap until first available price: median difference of only 3 days, and 99.48% of series are within 7 days (Phase 3, series_leading_zero_and_price_gap.csv). This is the strongest evidence in the whole EDA for treating early-life zeros differently from later intermittent zeros.
potential_risk_leakage: LOW risk - first_priced_date is a historical fact fixed before the origin date in almost all practical cases (item introductions in the forecast horizon itself would need care).

feature: category / department / store / state (static hierarchy fields)
purpose: Let the model share statistical strength within, and distinguish behavior across, hierarchy groups
why_it_may_help: Substantial and consistent behavioral differences exist across every level of the hierarchy
evidence_from_eda: Zero% ranges from 58.6% (FOODS_3) to 88.4% (HOBBIES_2) by department (Phase 3). Mean sales, seasonality_cv (p50 0.26 vs p90 0.56, Phase 8), SNAP sensitivity, and event sensitivity all vary materially by category/department/store (Phases 2,3,4,5,6,8).
potential_risk_leakage: None - static identifiers, always known.

purpose: Identify which series are strongly seasonal vs flat
data_source: sales_long_full.parquet (self) - CV of monthly mean sales
why_it_may_help: Lets a model or segmentation strategy treat highly seasonal items differently from steady sellers
evidence_from_eda: Per-series seasonality CV spans a wide range: p10=0.136, p50=0.263, p90=0.557 (Phase 8) - genuine heterogeneity, not a uniform pattern.
potential_risk_leakage: HIGH risk if computed on the full series history (including the forecast period) - must be computed using only pre-origin history.
